title: CRISPR RNA architecture steers Cas9 catalysis and fidelity via a guide repeat clasp motif.
data_url: https://academic.oup.com/nar/article-lookup/doi/10.1093/nar/gkag710#supplementary-data (retrieved as gkag710_supplemental_files.zip via Europe PMC supplementaryFiles for PMC13473882)

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded the 14 MB supplement archive from Europe PMC, unzipped it (one 13 MB PDF of supplementary figures plus 'Supplemental Tables S1-S3.xlsx', 38 KB) and parsed the spreadsheet with pandas. Table S2 = exactly 255 data rows, columns Assay, Protospacer (all 20 nucleotides), %EE_2part (percent editing efficiency with the two-part dual guide), %EE_sgRNA, delta; zero missing values, 255 unique protospacers, and delta equals %EE_2part minus %EE_sgRNA exactly. Table S1 = 122 synthesised RNA/DNA oligo sequences; Table S3 = 12 on/off-target genomic sites with coordinates. No symmetric cut-off on delta reproduces the paper's 68/43/144 class counts (at +/-3 I get 76/51/128; at +/-4, 57/46/152). Six dual-guide and five single-guide values exceed 100% editing, i.e. normalisation overshoot.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: That editing was measured in Jurkat cells by rhAmpSeq amplicon sequencing of indels after ribonucleoprotein electroporation; replicate structure for the 255-target screen; the cryo-EM structures (Protein Data Bank 8G1T, 8FZT, 9B2K); and all biochemical, nanopore off-target and molecular-dynamics results, which appear only as figures in the PDF, not as tables.

a1_downloadable.note: Supplement downloads without login from Europe PMC; licence is Creative Commons Attribution 4.0. I opened the spreadsheet itself.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Editing efficiency for both guide architectures, and their difference, are literal columns in Table S2 (%EE_2part, %EE_sgRNA, delta). Verified in the file.

a3_inputs_present.note: The 20-nucleotide protospacer sequence is present for all 255 rows; no accession lookups needed. Verified in the file.

a4_units_stated.note: Column names state percent editing efficiency (%EE); table title names the assay (rhAmpSeq). Minor caveat: 11 values exceed 100%.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL. Only 255 labelled rows, counted in the file. The checklist needs about 1,500 for regression or about 400 for classification; 255 is below both, and the three-class version gives roughly 40-70 examples per minority class.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially fits; no GPU needed. Verified by download.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: The 255-row count matches the paper, but the paper's architecture-preference classes (68 dual-guide-favouring, 43 single-guide-favouring, 144 comparable) cannot be reproduced from the delta column by any symmetric threshold I tried, and no class column or criterion is supplied.

a8_label_provenance.note: Labels are measured percentages of sequencing reads carrying insertions or deletions (rhAmpSeq), not a model output; the delta is arithmetic on two measurements. Verified that delta = dual minus single exactly.

existing_models.name: DeepSpCas9 (Kim et al., Science Advances 2019; convolutional network for SpCas9 single-guide activity)
existing_models.score_and_split: Search results state it was trained on measured activity at 12,832 target sequences from a human cell library and is reported as a strong ranker of guide activity; I did not retrieve the paper's own split-by-split numbers.

existing_models.name: CRISPRon (Xiang et al., Nature Communications 2021; deep learning with data integration)
existing_models.score_and_split: Search results describe it as performing well at ranking guide activity on large homogeneous datasets; exact numbers not retrieved.

existing_models.name: DeepCRISTL (Bioinformatics 2024; transfer learning for cell-context-specific on-target efficiency)
existing_models.score_and_split: Described in search results as using deep transfer learning to adapt on-target efficiency prediction to specific cellular contexts; numbers not retrieved.

existing_models.name: PLM-CRISPR (Bioinformatics 2025; protein language model ESM-2 fused with guide RNA sequence for cross-variant activity)
existing_models.score_and_split: Search results say each sample is a 59-nucleotide RNA (20-nt protospacer, 3-nt PAM, 36-nt scaffold) paired with a Cas9 variant sequence and an activity value; numbers not retrieved.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Not retrieved, but the framing implies activity prediction for new Cas9 variants is the open part.

existing_models.name: crisprHAL (Nature Communications 2023; transfer learning from small high-quality datasets)
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported in search results as improving guide activity prediction via transfer learning with small amounts of high-quality data, generalising across bacteria.

backbone.name: RNA-FM or a nucleotide language model (Nucleotide Transformer / DNABERT-2) over the 20-nucleotide protospacer
backbone.hardware: Laptop CPU; 255 short sequences embed in minutes
backbone.licence: Backbones permissive to non-commercial; data is Creative Commons Attribution 4.0

integration.partner_dataset: Published single-guide activity datasets (DeepSpCas9's 12,832 measured target sequences; CRISPRon training data)
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Does any sequence or predicted-structure feature explain when a two-part dual guide out-edits a fused single guide, a question the single-guide-only public datasets cannot address because they never varied the guide architecture?

controls.positive_control: Predict GC content or homopolymer length from the protospacer (must be near-perfect), and check that the model recovers the known preference for G at the position adjacent to the PAM in absolute editing efficiency.
controls.negative_control: Shuffle the delta column and confirm performance collapses to the global mean; the paper's own result (Pearson r = 0.22, R-squared = 0.05 for its composite structural score) is effectively a pre-existing near-null benchmark.
controls.external_validation: The 15 resynthesised unmodified guides (Supplementary Fig. S2, figure only, not tabulated) and the 12 endogenous on/off-target sites in Table S3 — both far too small to validate anything.

honest_claim_h3: Any model here could only claim: among 255 commercially pre-designed, already-highly-active spacers (median editing about 94%) tested once in Jurkat cells with chemically modified guides, sequence features predict the dual-versus-single guide editing difference this well — a claim limited by 255 rows, one cell line, one lab and one assay.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a guide RNA's 20-letter targeting sequence to predict whether two-piece or fused guide RNA edits that site better.
plain_idea.train_on: Each example is one 20-nucleotide targeting sequence (spacer) plus features computed from it; there are 255 examples, a count I verified by opening the spreadsheet.
plain_idea.predict: The difference in percent of DNA molecules carrying an edit between the natural two-part guide and the fused single guide, measured by amplicon sequencing of insertions and deletions in Jurkat cells.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Anyone ordering CRISPR reagents picks one guide format blindly; a predictor would tell them which to buy. Even a failure confirms the paper's conclusion that the choice is not sequence-encoded.

more_or_better_data.why: Our usable table is 255 matched pairs; DeepSpCas9 alone was trained on measured activity at 12,832 target sequences. The only thing unique here is the guide architecture comparison, and it exists for just those 255 spacers.

confidence_score.why: The 255-target screen is reported as single aggregate percentages per architecture with no replicate columns in the file, so per-prediction uncertainty cannot be grounded in measured noise.

models_beatable.why: The in-paper benchmark is weak (a multiple-regression composite structural score, Pearson r = 0.22, R-squared = 0.05) and is trivially beatable in principle, but it was fitted on the same 255 rows, so beating it on 255 rows proves little.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Public datasets (DeepSpCas9, CRISPRon) measure single-guide activity only, in different cell lines and assays, and never measure the dual-versus-single difference, so they cannot supply more of the same quantity; the condition 'new data measures the same quantity the same way' fails.

label_elsewhere.sources: Searched for public guide-architecture comparisons and found none; large public resources (DeepSpCas9's 12,832 measured targets, CRISPRon, CRISPR screen repositories) report single-guide activity only, never a matched dual-guide measurement.
label_elsewhere.why: The quantity to predict here — the editing difference between two guide RNA architectures — is measured nowhere else, so there is no external training or validation set to rescue the 255-row sample size.

ml_idea: Predict the dual-guide-minus-single-guide editing difference (delta %EE) from the 20-nucleotide protospacer, using a frozen RNA or DNA language model embedding plus a small regression head, benchmarked against the paper's own composite structural score (Pearson r = 0.22). Dead on arrival at 255 rows: with roughly 40-70 examples in each minority preference class, grouped cross-validation would give confidence intervals wider than any effect.

effort.compute_note: Measured directly: the whole dataset is a 38 KB spreadsheet with 255 rows of 20-nucleotide sequences, already parsed in this evaluation; embedding 255 short sequences on a CPU takes minutes.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the rows of Supplementary Table S2 — it is 255, below the Part A5 minimum. Done in five minutes, and it kills the project.

verdict_reason: The data is pristine and genuinely unique — 255 matched dual-guide versus single-guide editing measurements, labels already as columns, units stated, zero missing values — but 255 rows fails A5 outright, and the label exists in no other dataset so it cannot be topped up. A7 also wobbles: the paper's 68/43/144 preference classes cannot be reproduced from the delta column by any threshold. The paper's own conclusion is that the signal is not sequence-encoded (R-squared = 0.05), so the most likely outcome is an underpowered confirmation of a published null.
